findings.statement: D-065 OBLIGATION 1 (atomically bind one spawned agent_id to one run, assignment and digest) HOLDS on the bytes at HEAD 4ec13b5, and every arm of it is pinned by an executable fixture that dies when the guard is deleted. Re-derived from code, not from the report. THE ATOMIC PRIMITIVE: `.codex/hooks/subagent_stop_validate.py:121` takes `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` on `.agent-harness/admissions/<run>/.agent-locks/<agent>.lock`, opened with `O_CREAT|O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW` (so a planted symlink becomes ELOOP, not a lock on another inode). main() acquires it BEFORE the `conflicting_agent_assignment` ledger read it guards (call site at :402 is inside `consume_under_agent_lock`, which the lock wraps) and releases it in a `finally` by closing the descriptor, so kernel-on-death release makes 'released on every failure path' structural rather than a discipline. MUTATION (guard deletion): replacing the flock call with `pass` is killed by `test_hooks.py::test_concurrent_stops_by_one_agent_consume_exactly_one_assignment`. THE MINT-TIME GUARD: `.agent-harness/scripts/admit_agent.py:493` refuses a second mint for an expect_agent_id already holding an open-or-consumed receipt for a different assignment. MUTATION: `if conflict_assignment_id:` -> `if False:` is killed by `test_admit_agent_refuses_second_assignment_for_same_agent_id` AND by `test_one_agent_bound_in_one_run_is_still_admissible_in_another` -- the second kill is the one that matters, because it proves the per-run scope ceiling is pinned in the permissive direction too, not just the restrictive one. THE STOP-TIME LEDGER ENFORCEMENT: the `if conflict_assignment_id:` block at subagent_stop_validate.py:407. MUTATION -> `if False:` is killed by `test_subagentstop_blocks_agent_id_already_consumed_a_different_assignment`, while `test_subagentstop_ledger_conflict_check_ignores_same_assignment_restop` still passes, so the idempotent re-stop carve-out is separately pinned. No arm of obligation 1 survived deletion.

findings.statement: D-065 OBLIGATION 2 (make receipt/lease creation failure a hard Start failure) HOLDS at HEAD 4ec13b5 in both halves, each with a fixture that dies on guard deletion, AND the false-positive control is itself pinned. LEASE HALF: subagent_start_context.py:781-793 catches the lease-write OSError, sets lease_note to 'NOT RECORDED (...)' and appends to `start_errors`, which line 865 renders as `Hook preflight: FAIL - ...`. MUTATION: deleting the `start_errors.append(...)` (leaving the note) is killed by BOTH `test_subagentstart_hard_fails_when_lease_cannot_be_written` and `test_subagentstart_separates_a_lease_failure_from_a_healthy_receipt` -- so the fixtures pin the ERROR channel, not merely the cosmetic note. RECEIPT HALF AT START: `orphaned_mints` (:440-481) is now called unconditionally at :649, outside any `if not matches:`, and the round-7 qualification is that an orphan is cleared only by an admitting receipt FOR THAT SAME ASSIGNMENT (`assignment_id != admitted_assignment_id` at :474). MUTATION A (guard off): `return bound_to_this_agent, token_only` -> `return [], []` is killed by FOUR fixtures at once -- test_subagentstart_hard_fails_on_an_orphaned_mint, test_subagentstart_hard_fails_when_a_valid_receipt_masks_an_orphaned_mint, test_subagentstart_hard_fails_on_an_unattributable_token_only_mint, test_subagentstart_flags_the_new_agent_when_a_reopen_fails. MUTATION B (guard over-broad, i.e. the qualification removed): dropping `and assignment_id != admitted_assignment_id` is killed by `test_subagentstart_passes_when_the_open_mint_is_the_receipt_it_holds`. That two-sided kill is the important one: it proves the load-bearing claim in the record's round-7/8 section -- that an unqualified universal check would fail every healthy in-flight agent -- is enforced by a real fixture and not merely argued. CREATION-TIME HALF: admit_agent.py `fail()` raises SystemExit (non-zero) on both write failures, ledger-first then receipt-second at :698-708. MUTATION: replacing the receipt-write `fail(...)` with `pass` is killed by `test_admit_agent_fails_closed_when_the_receipt_cannot_be_written`; replacing the ledger-append `fail(...)` with `pass` is killed by `test_admit_agent_fails_closed_when_ledger_cannot_be_written`. THE RESIDUAL THE RECORD STATES IS ACCURATE AT HEAD, verified by reading the code rather than the paragraph: because the ledger append precedes the receipt write, a failed LEDGER append leaves nothing at all on disk, so Start legitimately reports 'none found' and PASSes; the compensating controls are the non-zero exit at creation time and Stop's refusal to admit any result without a matching open receipt.
assumptions_used: `Hook preflight: FAIL` is treated as load-bearing in the sense the code makes it: it is injected text plus a `systemMessage` warning. The durable record of it, `spawn_contract.subagent_start_preflight`, is SELF-REPORTED by the agent and merely required to equal 'PASS' by validate_result_contract (_harness.py:336). The B6 commit message states this limitation itself; obligation 2's teeth at Stop come from the lease and receipt requirements, not from the preflight string.

findings.statement: D-065 OBLIGATION 4 (pass a REPLACEMENT LIVE OVERLAPPING-RUN CANARY with unique write attribution) DOES NOT HOLD at HEAD 4ec13b5: the C6 canary is STALE, by the chain's own written rule and by arithmetic I performed on HEAD's bytes. C6's attestation `.agent-harness/runs/run-20260729-f10-d070-canary-c6/artifacts/ACTIVE_RUN_BRACKET_AROUND_CONSUME.json` pins TWO hook digests, deliberately: `stop_hook_sha256 0533da88...` and `start_hook_sha256 af8f7016...`, both taken at commit d564821. At HEAD the stop hook is still 0533da88..., but the START HOOK IS 8b28351235d32bb74c7bb84ee32acf910f2bccb4eef993bfbf86baecc6522d17, NOT af8f7016... . `git log --oneline d564821..HEAD -- .codex/hooks/subagent_start_context.py` returns exactly one commit: 7157bbe, the D-070 Part B6 fix, which changed 138 lines of that file. THIS IS THE EXACT DEFECT CLASS C5 WAS REJECTED FOR AT ROUND 7, and C6's own artifact writes the rule it now violates: 'Canary staleness is structural and is now a written rule: the canary is the LAST act before the sealing commit.' C6 was sealed at 4305533; two further commits landed after it (c2d1113, 7157bbe) and the second one moved a hook byte underneath it. THE CHANGE IS NOT ARGUABLY IMMATERIAL: 7157bbe rewrote `describe_admission_receipt`, which is on the very Start path C6 attested -- C6's own raw_logs/start_out.json records the line 'Admission receipt: open, bound to assignment A-D070-CANARY-C6', produced by that function. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT: there is NO automated staleness detector. `grep -rln start_hook_sha256` over the repository (excluding venv/.git) returns zero .py files -- no test, hook, validator or checker anywhere reads `start_hook_sha256`, `stop_hook_sha256`, `ACTIVE_RUN_BRACKET_AROUND_CONSUME` or `CANARY_ATTESTATION`. The only hits are two run-evidence JSON artifacts. So obligation 4 is enforced by human recomputation once per round, and by the assignment's own standard -- a guard whose deletion breaks no test is not verified -- it has no guard at all: nothing can be deleted, because nothing exists. Obligation 4 has now gone stale on four consecutive canaries (C1, C4, C5, C6) for the same structural reason, and the fix each time was a fresh canary rather than a check that would notice.
assumptions_used: The staleness standard applied is the chain's own, taken from the C6 artifact's `supersedes` field and from the C5 rejection at round 7, not one I invented: a canary whose pinned hook digest no longer matches HEAD is stale.
I did not re-run the canary; obligation 4 asks whether a passing canary stands against current bytes, and the digest comparison settles that without re-execution.

counterevidence_refs: C6's substantive attestation is otherwise sound and I found no defect in it: 36 ms bracket, pointer named the decoy at both ends, expected_agent_id enforced, consumed_by_agent_id=d070-canary-c6, result digest pinned in the append-only ledger, and the second-resolution limit of `consumed_at` disclosed rather than glossed. A reviewer could argue the B6 start-hook change touches receipt classification rather than lease sealing and so cannot affect the overlap property. I reject that as a rescue because (a) the change is on the Start path C6 exercised and logged, and (b) round 7 rejected C5 on a moved digest without any materiality carve-out, so accepting one here would be a standard applied more leniently to the canary that is currently convenient.

findings.statement: THE DIRECTED B6 QUESTION -- did the round-8 reordering create a path where a receipt error and a ledger error are both present and the WRONG ONE WINS? -- answers NO on the bytes at HEAD, and the answer is pinned by mutation in both directions. `describe_admission_receipt` now calls `classify_receipt_matches` at :613 BEFORE acting on `ledger_errors` at :618, and the ledger-error return is `errors + [ledger complaint]` (:639-646) -- the receipt's own errors are CARRIED, not replaced. Every element of `start_errors` is then joined into the single `Hook preflight: FAIL - ...` line at :865, so both errors reach the operator and the verdict is FAIL under either cause; `receipt_verdict_is_fatal` (:616) is used only to decide whether the NOTE is overwritten by 'MINT FAILED', never to decide the verdict. MUTATION A (regress the fix): changing the return to `[] + [ledger complaint]`, i.e. discarding the receipt errors exactly as the pre-B6 ordering did, is killed by `test_subagentstart_keeps_a_fatal_receipt_verdict_when_the_ledger_is_broken`. MUTATION B (the rule the coordinator proposed and the fix lane refused): changing `if ledger_errors:` to `if ledger_errors and not admitted_assignment_id:`, so a valid open receipt clears the ledger denial, is killed by `test_subagentstart_fails_on_a_malformed_ledger_beside_a_valid_receipt`. Both fixtures are on-topic and named for the behaviour they pin, and that fixture's Controls A/B/C are real: A shows the malformed row is the only thing separating FAIL from PASS, B builds a second tree where orphaning A and garbling only A's row would print PASS under the proposed rule, C shows Stop blocks the same agent anyway so a Start downgrade would only postpone the refusal. I could not construct a case where the verdict is wrong.
assumptions_used: 'The wrong one wins' is read as either (a) the reported VERDICT being decided by the wrong error, or (b) a fatal error being silently dropped from the operator-visible channel. Both were tested; neither occurs.

findings.statement: THE DIRECTED SSOT QUESTION -- can the executable measurement vocabulary report a NUMBER where it should report an ERROR? -- answers YES, and the hole is the exact one the B6 commit and the module docstring cite as their reason for rejecting the shell form. check_ssot_consistency.py's docstring, reason 3 for refusing `subprocess`, reads: '`grep -c` exits 1 and prints 0 when nothing matches. A mistyped pattern would therefore report the number zero rather than an error -- silence presenting as data, which is the failure mode this whole file exists to refuse.' The replacement reproduces it exactly: `_count_lines_matching` (:1078-1096) ends `return sum(1 for line in text.splitlines() if regex.search(line))`, which is 0 for a pattern that COMPILES BUT MATCHES NOTHING, and `check_facts` (:1342-1354) treats any non-None return as a successful measurement, erroring only on `measured != current`. There is no 'matched nothing' arm anywhere in the closed vocabulary, and no fixture for one -- test_ssot_consistency.py covers unknown kind, unknown key, missing key, unreadable target, escaping path, absolute path, invalid pattern and malformed JSON, but NOT the zero-match case. EXECUTED, NOT ARGUED: in the scratch tree I set hook_fixture_count's pattern to `^def NOSUCHTHING_` (valid regex, zero matches) and its value to 0, and updated the four live surfaces that assert 108 (SHARED_CONTEXT.md, VALIDATION_LEDGER.md x2, the D-067 report). The checker returned EXIT 0, `ok: true`, `errors: []`, and `fact_measurements: {"hook_fixture_count": 0}` -- a number reported for a measurement that measured nothing. The only thing standing between that state and today's repository is that the declared value happens to be non-zero and the cross-surface assertions happen to disagree; the cross-surface check is the OLD mechanism, the one B6 was written because it is insufficient. So the measurement layer executes, which is a genuine improvement over the prose it replaced, but it cannot distinguish 'I measured and found none' from 'I measured nothing'. On a single-writer update -- the flow this repository actually uses, where SSOT_FACTS.json and its surfaces move in one commit -- that distinction is the whole guard.
assumptions_used: A zero-valued fact is treated as reachable rather than absurd: the vocabulary imposes no positivity constraint (`check_facts` requires only `isinstance(current, int)`), and `count_lines_matching` is generic over any file and pattern, so nothing confines it to counts that must be non-zero.

Severity is medium, not high: no current fact is misreported (both measure correctly today -- 136 and 108), so this is a latent hole in a checker, not a live falsehood, and it does not by itself move any of the four obligations.
evidence_refs: .agent-harness/tests/test_ssot_consistency.py:958-1090 (the F-SSOT-10 fixtures; no zero-match case among them)
counterevidence_refs: The B6 change is a real improvement and I do not want this finding read as a reversal of it: before B6 the declared count sat two behind reality while the checker printed ok:true, and executing the measurement closes that. `json_array_length` has no equivalent hole -- a missing key, a non-array target and malformed JSON are each an explicit error.

In today's repository the drift check does fire: with the pattern mistyped but the declared value left at 108, the checker reports 'measures 0 in the working tree' and exits non-zero. The hole opens only when the declared value and the measurement are wrong together, which is exactly what a single-writer commit produces.

findings.statement: THE RECORD IS AGAIN AHEAD OF THE CODE at HEAD 4ec13b5, in the section written at round 8 specifically to stop that happening, and in the two numbers a gate decision would read first.
